title.narrative: Promoting Gender Equality in Housing Finance Project

description.narrative:
1. The project is aligned with the following impact: gender equity promotion and sustainable economic growth achieved. The project will have the following outcome: acquisition and renovation of housing units by women increased.
2. The project will deliver the following outputs: Output 1: Long-term affordable mortgage financing for eligible women borrowers made available. Through the ADB loan HCSBK will provide mortgage loans exclusively targeted at women borrowers to finance at least 3,000 women; Output 2: Accessibility to HCSBK's lending products for eligible women borrowers improved; HCSBK will adopt a gender policy and will conduct at least three nationwide public awareness campaigns on housing finance products for women; Output 3: Gender inclusiveness of the banking sector's housing finance assessed. This output will be delivered by conducting a nationwide study on women's access to housing and finance products which will have to be endorsed by the government.
3. ADB will provide HCSBK with an FIL of $100 million equivalent. HCSBK will use the tenge proceeds from ADB to offer affordable residential mortgage finance exclusively to women customers, each acting as the sole borrower and bearer of the legal title to a residential housing unit. The mortgage subloans provided by HCSBK will be used for the acquisition of residential housing units or the renovation of existing homes. A minimum of 60% of the proceeds from the ADB loan will be allocated to provide mortgage loans to female borrowers located in rural regions, i.e., those outside of the four large cities with the lowest poverty rates: Aktau, Almaty, Atyrau and Nur-Sultan. While the maximum monthly income level per household has been set at T320,000, at least 20% of all mortgage loans financed by the ADB loan will be to low-income female borrowers with a monthly household income of less than T200,000. A price ceiling of T30 million will apply for housing units that can be financed under the ADB project, as well as a ceiling of T3.7 million for renovation loans.

description.narrative: Acquisition and renovation of housing units by women increased.

By the end of 2022: a. 8% annual growth rate in the lending portfolio to women (2019-2022), reaching at least 28,000 mortgage loans issued by HCSBK to women borrowers (2018 baseline: 20,622). Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved.
Since the beginning of 2020, following the effectiveness of the loan in November 2020, the bank has issued more than 28,000 loans annually. In total, Otbasy bank issued 156,158 subloans to women over the last four years.

With the consistent increase in the number of women issued loans, Otbasy bank was able to achieve post a double-digit growth rate in the last three years.

Despite not reaching the targets of 1% annual growth rate which was envisaged to result in a 59% share of women in the outstanding loan portfolio, substantial increase has been achieved. Outstanding loans to women more than doubled from T697 billion (2020) to T1.64 trillion (2023).

HCSBK develops at least one financial product exclusively targeted at women borrowers (2019 baseline:NA) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. Umai Women's Mortgage Program was developed by Otbasy Bank and launched for implementation in April 2021. Output: Accessibility to HCSBK?s lending products for eligible women borrowers improved Indicator: 2b. HCSBK adopts a gender policy (2019 baseline: NA) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. In September 2023, the Bank approved new Regulations on Diversity and Inclusivity and the Rules on Gender Aspects. These measures were adopted based on ADB's recommendations. An annual Action Plan for Gender Equality for 2023 was also developed and approved, leading to the integration of gender considerations into the Bank's Code of Business Ethics, Personnel Policy, Sustainable Development Policy, and the Strategy for 2024-2033. Additionally, job descriptions for all employees now include compliance with the Diversity and Inclusivity Regulations. The Chairman of the Bank, Lyazzat Yerkenovna Ibragimova, was appointed Commissioner for Diversity and Inclusivity, including on Gender Aspects in Otbasy Bank, by the Order No. 624 as of 6 November 2023. Data Source: HCSBK's internal and monitoring reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Y Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Y Target year: 2022 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Gender inclusiveness of the banking sector?'s housing finance assessed Indicator: 3. Results of a nationwide study on women's access to housing and finance products disseminated and endorsed by the government (2019 baseline: NA) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. Four consultants consisting of an International Housing Finance Expert, International Gender Specialist, National Gender Specialist, a National Researcher (Statistician), and a national survey firm were mobilized to develop the study. The results, including the review of operations through a gender lens, were cascaded and disseminated to Otbasy management and staff in October 2022 through a 3-day seminar workshop. In January 2024, the Ministry of National Economy endorsed the nationwide study.
